newsitem.title: UK: Four green rates to devalue on Wednesday - HGCA.
newsitem.headline: Four green rates to devalue on Wednesday - HGCA.

text.p: The green rates of the mark, Belgian franc, guilder and the Austrian schilling will be devalued in the European Union's (EU) agrimonetary grid on Wednesday, the UK Home-Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA) said on Tuesday.

It calculated that the green mark would be devalued to 1.93805 per Ecu from 1.93473, the green Belgian franc to 39.9502 from 39.8740, the green guilder to 2.17413 from 2.17067 and the green schilling to 13.6364 from 13.6155.
The changes were triggered by the relative strength of the Irish pound and sterling in the system both of which are forecast to be revalued in January.

The HGCA said the green rate of the Irish pound would enter the third of possibly five 10-day confirmation periods for a revaluation on January 11. The green sterling meanwhile would start the second confirmation period for a revaluation on January 21.
Green rates are used in calculating EU farm subsidies in national currencies and have no direct impact on currency markets.
